meaning: Stipulative finite decision-table controls, not a free-will theory. Reusing fixedConditionsStable, a fixed pair of law and complete input plus an exact response function entails stable selected output. In the displayed finite table, equal law and input imply equal action; an unconstrained actual history has no different action at the same context. Changing the input alone or the law alone gives explicit different actions. A constrained history and the unconstrained actual history share their action. A second, single relational law permits both Boolean actions at the very same unconstrained input, while requiring the true action at every constrained input. Thus lawfulness need not be functionality; nondeterministic lawful alternatives need not violate a law. Complete means complete for this stipulated table. No physical realization, freedom, responsibility, metaphysical adequacy or root premise is established.
